correctness.rationale: The exact odd-binomial harmonic identity n!P_n(-1)=S_n=sum_{j=1}^n 2^(j-1)/j follows by parity filtering two standard binomial integrals. The convergent 2-adic logarithm series Σ_{j>=1}2^(j-1)/j=-(1/2)log(-1)=0 makes S_N=-2^N R(N), R(N)=Σ_{r>=1}2^(r-1)/(N+r). Legendre ν_2(N!)=N-s_2(N), complete odd-residue-cycle products for U((a2^e)!) and uniform tail valuation bounds establish R(a2^e+Δ)→R(Δ) and U((a2^e+Δ)!)→U_a U(Δ!). This proves the exact stated 2-adic limit for each fixed a>=1, Δ>=0; S_Δ positive rational for Δ>=1 gives nonzero limit, Δ0 is zero. Independent exact rational n<=35 checks and modular 2-adic samples corroborate, not prove uniform generality.
residual_risks: Bounded independent computation is corroborative only; the all-parameter proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The -1 input is a mathematically motivated first negative argument of a natural p-adic partial Stirling family and is outside the input range of the familiar limit theorem. An exact nonzero limit for every shift and dyadic multiplier, derived from p-adic log cancellation, supplies usable boundary data for the partial-Stirling zero/limit problem. This is narrow but is not a routine parameter substitution because negative exponents invalidate the previously cited theorem.
residual_risks: Mathematical value is judged for the final submitted original theorem, not merely computational reproducibility.
